newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles County warned $51.7 mln in jeopardy.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles County warned $51.7 mln in jeopardy.

text.p: A Los Angeles County official warned Tuesday that the county may lose $51.7 million in funding for fire protection because of Proposition 218, and urged the county to come up with a plan to avert a shortfall.

The $51.7 million, raised through the fire department's fire suppression benefit assessment, has been "jeopardized" by the passage of the proposition, Zev Yaroslavsky, chairman of the county Board of Supervisors, said in a motion.
Proposition 218, approved by California voters last November, strengthened state law to require that most local taxes be submitted to voters for approval.
If the $51.7 million is lost, Yaroslavsky warned that the county's ability to provide fire protection services to 3.1 million residents in 51 cities could be compromised.

"This board desires to maintain the current level of fire protection services to ensure public safety," he said. "All funding options must be examined and made available in time to meet legal requirements and ensure continued funding for public safety."
He urged the Board of Supervisors to approve a motion Tuesday instructing budget officials to review the county's options to replace any losses in fire protection funding.
Yaroslavsky's motion calls on county budget officials to report back to the board with their recommendations in time to place the issue on the June 3 ballot.
